test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 11 Jun, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: One pipe can fill the tank in 18 minutes while another pipe can empty the completely filled tank in 19 minutes. If both the pipes are operated together on empty tank, how long (in minutes) will it take to fill one-third of the tank?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net rate of filling = 1/18 − 1/19 = 1/(18 × 19) = 1/342 tank per minute.

Time to fill full tank = 342 minutes.

Time to fill 1/3 of the tank = 342 ÷ 3 = 114 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 114 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 **Pipe**
 **Time (min)**
 **Total Capacity (LCM)**
 **Efficiency**

 **Filling Pipe**
 18
 342 units
 +19

 **Emptying Pipe**
 19
 −18

⇒ **Combined Efficiency** = 19 − 18 = 1 unit/min

⇒ **Target Volume** (1/3 of tank) = 342 ÷ 3 = 114 units

⇒ **Time Required** = Target Volume ÷ Combined Efficiency

⇒ **Time Required** = 114 ÷ 1 = 114 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 114 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns Logic

Filling pipes have **positive efficiency** while emptying pipes (leaks) have **negative efficiency**.

Net Work Formula

If pipe A fills in x and pipe B empties in y, net time T = (x × y) ÷ (y − x) for one full tank.

Fractional Work

To find time for a fraction k of the tank, **Timeₖ = k × Total Time**.</p
